articles.title: Who owns the patch? Name who applies the fix before you verify it
articles.excerpt: Who owns the patch? Name who applies the fix before you verify it In October, exploited flaws in PHP, BeyondTrust Remote Support and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator all reached CISA's Known Exploited Vu…
articles.body: Who owns the patch? Name who applies the fix before you verify it In October, exploited flaws in PHP, BeyondTrust Remote Support and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator all reached CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Our read: in each one, the safe answer depended on how the product was deployed: a vendor-hosted copy was patched by the vendor, a self-hosted copy had to be patched by its owner, and a copy bundled inside someone else's product can only be fixed by that vendor. Here is what each publisher said, the Patch-Owner Map (our proposal) step by step, and the questions to send a host or vendor so you get a version and a date back, not a yes. Our previous post was about the second pass after a patch: patch, then verify. This one is about the step before it.

By preparing an import.tf like the following and running tofu plan -generate-config-out=export.tf , you can export the current configuration. articles.title: MCP Monitoring: Why Your Agents Fail Silently and How to Catch It
articles.excerpt: Your MCP server is returning 200s. Your uptime dashboard is green. And an agent somewhere just told a user "I couldn't complete that request" for the fortieth time today. That gap is what MCP monitori…
articles.body: Your MCP server is returning 200s. Your uptime dashboard is green. And an agent somewhere just told a user "I couldn't complete that request" for the fortieth time today. That gap is what MCP monitoring is about. When an MCP server breaks, a person rarely sees an error page. An agent reads a failure, retries, picks a different tool, or gives up and summarizes the problem in natural language. None of that shows up in a classic HTTP monitor. This guide covers why MCP needs its own monitoring, which signals are worth capturing, the main tools you can use today, and a walkthrough of one hosted option. Why MCP monitoring is different from API monitoring Classic API monitoring assumes a request, a status code, and a human or a service that notices when things go wrong.

articles.body: Ein Kameramann, eine 13-Dollar-App und eine Frage, die viel größer ist Wenn ein Kameramann, der „Knives Out" gedreht hat, eine iPhone-App für 13 Dollar veröffentlicht, ist die Aufmerksamkeit garantiert. Steve Yedlins Chromagraph Camera verarbeitet Fotos mit derselben Farbmathematik, die er für Filmproduktionen nutzt. Die virale Reaktion dreht sich meist um Farbprofile und Film-Look. Die spannendere Frage liegt eine Ebene tiefer: Wenn sich das Bild so stark verändern lässt, ohne die Kamera auszutauschen – wie viel von dem, was wir „sehen", entsteht eigentlich erst im Kopf? Für Menschen mit Amblyopie (lazy eye) ist das keine akademische Frage. Das Problem mit „zu spät" Amblyopie entsteht, wenn das Gehirn das Signal eines Auges dauerhaft unterdrückt.

Ask Photos asks for calendar access and then hands the event to Android’s own confirmation prompt, suggesting it works with your default calendar app rather than just Google Calendar. The RAM crisis, driven by rising demand for AI infrastructure, has pushed prices up across the board, including smartphones. So far this year, Google and Samsung have raised prices, while other OEMs have been forced to make trade-offs to avoid that fate. But a RAM shortage may not be the only issue brands face heading into 2027, as Samsung’s OLED screens, which are used by several phone makers, could also become pricier.

articles.body: Faraway is the latest game from Steph Thirion, the solo developer behind 2009’s critically acclaimed iOS puzzler Eliss . (It’s published by Annapurna Interactive , the company arguably best-known for publishing offbeat games for wider audiences.) At a distance, Faraway looks like a small project: a high-score chasing arcade game about shooting stars. In reality, it’s a 16-year passion project that has finally come to fruition. Even in its one-button simplicity, Faraway feels like the kind of small-scale masterwork that so often gets overlooked in an industry that increasingly values Hollywood production over expressive gameplay.

articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower peaks tonight — and fireballs could steal the show
articles.excerpt: The Taurid meteor shower could spawn dazzling fireballs in the coming weeks! Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: Heads up stargazers! The Taurid meteor shower is upon us, bringing multiple peaks of activity that could see spectacular shooting stars and fireballs brighten November's sky. Here's where and when to look. What is the Taurid meteor shower(s)? Every autumn, Earth plows through streams of debris left behind by Comet Encke, a 3-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) ice body that orbits the sun once every 3.3 years. These debris streams produce two branches of the Taurid meteor shower : The Southern Taurids, active from Sept. 20 to Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids, active from Oct. 20 to Dec. 10. As Earth plows through the debris streams, tiny particles slam into our atmosphere at 65,000 miles per hour (104,607 kilometers per hour), producing dazzling streaks of light across the night sky.
